title: Median Wage Impact from AI by 2030
description: Projected change in real median wages in the US due to AI adoption, combining productivity gains and displacement effects.

sources.title: AI and the US Labor Market
Power and Progress: Our Thousand-Year Struggle Over Technology and Prosperity
sources.excerpt: Technology does not automatically benefit workers; shared prosperity requires deliberate policy choices. AI could follow historical pattern of concentrating gains among capital owners.

sources.title: Global Wage Report 2022-23: The impact of inflation and COVID-19 on wages and purchasing power
The Uneven Impact of Generative AI on Entrepreneurial Performance
sources.publisher: HBS Working Paper (Otis, Clarke, Delecourt, Holtz, Koning)
sources.excerpt: The paper reports no statistically significant average effect on revenues or profits. But effects are highly heterogeneous: high‑performing businesses at baseline appear to improve (roughly 15 percent), while low performers do worse (roughly 8-10 percent worse)

sources.title: AI Will Transform the Global Economy. Let's Make Sure It Benefits Humanity
sources.excerpt: In most scenarios, AI will likely worsen overall inequality. Higher-income workers may see disproportionate wage gains.

sources.title: UPS cuts 12,000 jobs, citing softer demand and higher union labor costs
sources.excerpt: UPS announced 12,000 job cuts, primarily management and salaried positions, as part of a $1 billion cost-reduction effort. Full-time driver pay raised to $49/hr top rate under 2023 Teamsters contract.

sources.title: Unbalanced labor market power is what makes technology — including AI — threatening to workers
sources.excerpt: AI is unlikely to be a direct threat to wages; the root causes of sluggish wage growth are policy decisions that led to imbalanced employer power. Productivity growth has not historically caused higher unemployment or inequality.

sources.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Labor Market
sources.excerpt: AI exposure is concentrated among high-skill, high-wage occupations, but wage effects may cascade downward.

sources.title: AI could be coming for higher-paid workers this time
Walmart Lowers Starting Pay for New Hires
sources.excerpt: Walmart's minimum starting wage is $14/hr while average U.S. associate wage reached $18.25 by 2025. The company invested in checkout and inventory automation but has not disclosed specific per-location staffing reduction figures.

sources.title: AI and the Extended Workday
sources.excerpt: When someone transitions to a job with high exposure to AI, they work 3.5 hours longer per week. Productivity gains captured by firms, not wages.

sources.title: Employment Cost Index — 2025 Q1
Automatic Reaction — What Happens to Workers at Firms that Automate?
sources.publisher: Review of Economics and Statistics (Bessen, Goos, Salomons, van den Berge)
sources.excerpt: Tenured workers cumulatively lose about 3,800 Euros in wage and salary earnings over five years on average (about 9% of one year's income). We find little change in wage rates.

sources.title: US Wage Tracker — Posted Wage Trends by Occupation
sources.excerpt: Posted wages for AI-exposed occupations (admin, data entry, basic accounting) grew 1.2% YoY vs. 4.1% for non-AI-exposed roles, suggesting wage suppression.

sources.title: Augmenting or Automating Labor?
sources.excerpt: Automation AI negatively impacts low-skilled wages; augmentation AI raises high-skilled wages.

sources.title: The Wage Compression that Persisted
Generative AI at Work
sources.excerpt: Access to AI assistance increases worker productivity, as measured by issues resolved per hour, by 15% on average, with substantial heterogeneity across workers.

sources.title: Steering Technological Progress
sources.excerpt: For the empirically plausible case that capital and labor are gross complements, raising wages requires capital-augmenting innovation rather than labor-augmenting.

sources.title: Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects
sources.excerpt: Workplaces that adopted AI chatbots showed no significant difference in employment, early-career jobs, job churn, or worker mix. Difference-in-differences estimates for earnings and wages are all precisely estimated zeros, ruling out effects larger than 2%.

sources.title: Expertise
sources.excerpt: automation can simultaneously replace experts in some occupations while augmenting expertise in others.

sources.title: How AI uncouples hard work from fair wages through surveillance pay
sources.publisher: Washington Center for Equitable Growth (Dubal, Negron)
sources.excerpt: Audit of 500 AI vendors finds surveillance pay spreading across healthcare, customer service, and logistics.

sources.title: Economic Growth under Transformative AI
sources.publisher: Annual Review of Economics / NBER (Korinek, Trammell)
sources.excerpt: Sufficiently advanced AI could dramatically raise growth rates and lower labor share, breaking Kaldor Facts. Wages may rise or fall depending on returns to scale and direction of technical change.

sources.title: Robots and Wages: A Meta-Analysis
sources.publisher: Structural Change and Economic Dynamics (Klump, Schneider, Jurkat)
sources.excerpt: The overall effect of industrial robots on wages is close to zero and insignificant. 53 papers, 2,143 estimations.

sources.title: PwC Global AI Jobs Barometer 2025
sources.excerpt: AI-skilled workers command a 56% wage premium, up from 25% in prior year. AI roles median compensation at $157K vs. $49,500 all-occupation median.

sources.title: Generative AI and Firm Productivity: Field Experiments in Online Retail
sources.excerpt: Large-scale field experiments find treatment effects 0-16.3% on sales, mapping directly into TFP improvements.

sources.title: Estimating AI Productivity Gains from Claude Conversations
sources.excerpt: Claude speeds up individual tasks by about 80%. Extrapolating suggests 1.8% annual US productivity growth over the next decade.

sources.title: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2024
sources.excerpt: Median annual wage for all occupations: $49,500. AI-exposed administrative and clerical wages grew 1.1% vs. 3.8% for non-AI-exposed occupations.

sources.title: The Wage Divide is Widening Again and AI May Be to Blame
sources.excerpt: Since January 2023, salaries at the top quartile of the wage distribution have grown by more than 30%. Over the same period, salaries at the bottom quartile have risen by only around 10%.

sources.title: AI Adoption by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
sources.publisher: OECD (Calvino, Bianchini, Lane, Montegu, Verger, Ancheva)
sources.excerpt: The United Kingdom and the United States may experience higher gains, ranging from 0.4 to 1.3 percentage points annually for the next 10 years.

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Economic Productivity
sources.excerpt: Each year of AI model progress reduced task time by 8%. Access to any AI model increased Earnings Per Minute by 81.3%. Continued scaling could boost US productivity by ~20% over the next decade.

sources.title: Resolving the Automation Paradox: Falling Labor Share, Rising Wages
sources.excerpt: falling labor share accounted for 16% of U.S. real wage growth between 1954 and 2019

sources.title: Labor Market Effects of Generative AI
sources.excerpt: Small positive wage effects identified for workers in AI-exposed occupations; adoption concentrated among younger, college-educated, higher-earning employees.

sources.title: O-Ring Automation
sources.excerpt: Labour income can rise under partial automation because automation scales the value of remaining bottleneck tasks.

sources.title: Can advanced AI lead to negative economic growth?
sources.excerpt: wages fall by 25%, and long-run welfare drops by 16.5%

sources.title: Past Automation and Future A.I.: How Weak Links Tame the Growth Explosion
sources.excerpt: Despite the accelerating growth, the effects of A.I. on GDP per person are remarkably small for the next 20 to 40 years.

sources.title: Generative AI and Firm Values
sources.excerpt: A one-standard-deviation increase in Generative AI exposure is associated with a 0.6% decline in the hourly wage rate. For occupations with exposure derived solely from core tasks, a one-standard-deviation higher Generative AI exposure corresponds to a significantly greater decline in relative wage rates by 1.4%.

sources.title: Task-Specific Technical Change and Comparative Advantage
sources.excerpt: raising average wages by 21 percent

sources.title: AI, Productivity, and Labor Markets: A Review of the Empirical Evidence
sources.excerpt: Small but statistically significant positive wage effects found across AI-exposed occupations; 35.9% of US workers used generative AI by December 2025.

sources.title: How AI is affecting productivity and jobs in Europe
sources.publisher: CEPR VoxEU (Aldasoro, Gambacorta, Pál, Revoltella, Weiss, Wolski)
sources.excerpt: AI adoption causally increases labour productivity levels by 4% on average. Employees in AI-using companies benefit through higher wages, both in total and per employee.

sources.title: AI is simultaneously aiding and replacing workers, wage data suggest
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas (J. Scott Davis)
sources.excerpt: For occupations with the median experience premium (40 percent), a one-standard-deviation increase in AI exposure is associated with a 0.05 percentage point decline in wage growth.

sources.title: AI is simultaneously aiding and replacing workers, wage data suggest
sources.excerpt: AI's impact depends on whether it automates or augments. For zero-experience-premium occupations, increased AI exposure is associated with -0.28pp reduction in wage growth. Wages in AI-exposed jobs not uniformly declining.

sources.title: Steering Technological Progress
sources.excerpt: Benefits of steering technology depend on complementarity to labor, relative income, and labor factor share.

sources.title: Nonfarm Business Sector Labor Productivity: 2.2% Above CBO Pre-Pandemic Forecast
sources.excerpt: Are we finally seeing AI in the productivity data? A big upward revision to earlier data and strong Q4 bring us 2.2% above CBO's pre-pandemic forecast. Annual rates: 1 year: 2.8%, 2 years: 2.5%, 6 years: 2.2%

sources.title: Pascual Restrepo on AI, Automation, and the Future of Work
sources.publisher: Yale Department of Economics (Restrepo, interviewed by Strathmann)
sources.excerpt: In research forthcoming in the Quarterly Journal of Economics, they examine how automation often targets tasks that pay workers wages above their outside options. When those tasks are automated, those wage 'rents' disappear, amplifying wage losses and contributing to rising inequality.

sources.title: Job Transformation, Specialization, and the Labor Market Effects of AI
sources.excerpt: average individual wages are roughly unchanged for incumbents of occupations with no AI exposure, rise by around 4% at moderate exposure, and drop by as much as 35% for workers in the most exposed occupations

sources.title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves
sources.excerpt: This estimate of the value of tasks in Claude.ai has dropped slightly from $49.3 to $47.9. US avg. hourly wage: $37.3.

sources.title: Will Wired Belts Become the New Rust Belts? AI and the Emerging Geography of American Job Risk
sources.publisher: Digital Planet, The Fletcher School, Tufts University
sources.excerpt: total income loss of between $200 billion to $1.5 trillion, representing 2% to 15% of overall income from wages and salaries across the U.S.

sources.title: AI Narrows Performance Gaps — But Does That Mean It Reduces Inequality?
sources.excerpt: whether it is, on net, an equalizing force remains a genuinely open question—one that the current evidence, important as it is, does not yet answer.

sources.title: Forecasting the Economic Effects of AI
sources.publisher: Forecasting Research Institute (w/ Fed Chicago, Yale, Stanford, UPenn)
sources.excerpt: In a rapid AI scenario, economists forecast labor income share dropping from ~58% to 45% by 2050, implying significant downward pressure on median wages even if aggregate GDP grows.

sources.title: Generative AI and Occupational Entry Barriers: The Labor-Supply Channel of Technological Change
sources.excerpt: The mean is 0.17 (SD 0.11), implying that for the average occupation, GenAI could reduce total work time by roughly 17 percent under this conservative calibration.

sources.title: Goldman Sachs on AI Agents and Labor Market Impact
sources.excerpt: Workers displaced from technology-disrupted occupations face more difficult short-run transitions back into employment. They take approximately one month longer to find a new job and suffer real earnings losses of more than 3% upon reemployment, compared with negligible losses for workers displaced from more stable occupations.

sources.title: Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First
sources.excerpt: Workers using AI might well agree that it's increasing their productivity without believing they're seeing the benefits.
